title: Mapusyaw soybean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Mapusyaw soybean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Mapusyaw soybean is a grain soybean variety. About 90 days to harvest, 2.2 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: Mapusyaw soybean is a grain soybean variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2001 as NSIC 2001 Sy 09. BPI Lbncrdc, Los Baños, Laguna bred it. It takes about 90 days from sowing to harvest, with 2.18 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

**Yield:** 2.18 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** the areas in its trials, in both the wet and the dry season.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Mapusyaw soybean takes about 90 days from sowing to harvest. That is 5.4 days longer than the average of the 19 grain soybean varieties with a day count, 84.6 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 2.18 t/ha beats the average of its group, 1.92. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit soybean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 18.4 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is straw yellow. The seed holds 33.6 percent crude protein.
Where and when to plant Mapusyaw soybean

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Grain soybean goes to feed and food processors, while vegetable soybean, or edamame, is picked green. Pick a variety rated against rust, the main soybean disease here.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 90 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 2.18 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Mapusyaw?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
